The data has a lot of numbers related to health. It includes economic data and health factors such as expenditures Hepatitis B, BMI, polio, and HIV/AIDS. I chose linear regression as the model to use on the data to see if these values had a linear affect on the life expectancy of the subjects.

# set the number of features for the plot
num_features = len(columns)

# Number of columns for displaying the plots
num_cols = 4

# Number of rows
num_rows = (num_features + num_cols -1) // num_cols

# Create a figure and set of subplots
fig, axes = plt.subplots(num_rows, num_cols, figsize = (15, num_rows * 5))

axes = axes.flatten()

# Create a plot graph for each feature
for i, col in enumerate(columns):
    sns.regplot(x=life_expectancy_raw[col], y=life_expectancy_raw['Life expectancy '] , order = 1, ax= axes[i])
    axes[i].set_title(f'{col} vs Life expectancy')
for i in range(num_features, num_rows * num_cols):
    fig.delaxes(axes[i])

# adjust layout to prevent overlap
plt.tight_layout()

# Show the plot
plt.show()

After doing a little cleaning of the data and then plotting prior to running the predictions I had some ideas. It might go without saying, but it looks like adult mortality directly correlates with life expectancy. I think that is to be expected. BMI seems to correlate as well, but there are some outliers and there seems to be a larger band of variance. For some reason schooling has a direct correlation as well. I interpret that to maean that people with higher educations tend to live longer. This is presumably due to lower risk jobs. Hepatitis B and Polio charts look almost identical.

# Create the dataframe with
df = life_expectancy_raw[[' BMI ', 'Total expenditure', " HIV/AIDS", 'Income composition of resources', 'Schooling', 'Life expectancy ']]

# Separate out the regressor values by removing 'Life Expectancy' which is the value we are trying to predict
regressors_values = df[[' BMI ', 'Total expenditure', " HIV/AIDS", 'Income composition of resources', 'Schooling']]

# Separate out the response values
response_values = df['Life expectancy ']

# Split the data into train test with a 20% test size and random rows
X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(regressors_values, response_values ,test_size=0.2, random_state=43)

# create a linear regression model
lr = LinearRegression()

# fit the data into the model
lr.fit(X_train, y_train)

# predictions made on test data
prediction=lr.predict(X_test)

# print predictions
print(prediction)
